location: Jebel Shams canyon (Wadi Nakhr), Ad Dakhiliyah Governorate
alt: Deep rock canyon on the Jebel Shams plateau rim in the Western Hajar
caption: The canyon rim at Jebel Shams, where the plateau at about 2,000 m drops roughly 1,000 m into Wadi Nakhr. It is the inland Oman this trip is built around: two tent nights on the rim, with the Balcony Walk starting a short drive away.

alt: Stone-walled terrace steps cut into the canyon side along the Balcony Walk on Jebel Shams
caption: Terrace steps cut into the canyon side beside the W6 Balcony Walk, which follows the wall with no guardrails and the full drop on one side. The trail is listed as about 7-8 km return and 3-4 hours: easy underfoot but not for anyone uneasy with heights.

location: Sab Bani Khamis, Wadi Nakhr, Jebel Shams
alt: Abandoned stone houses of Sab Bani Khamis clinging to the canyon wall
caption: Sab Bani Khamis, the abandoned terrace village at the end of the Balcony Walk. Its stone houses and tiny fields hang on a ledge in the canyon wall, a record of how mountain communities lived before roads reached the Hajar.

location: Wadi Bani Awf mountain road, Al Batinah South / Ad Dakhiliyah
alt: Narrow mountain road winding through the rock walls of Wadi Bani Awf
caption: The Wadi Bani Awf crossing links the Batinah side of the Hajar to Balad Sayt and Al Hamra. Steep sections, narrow ledges and no passing room make it the driving test of the trip, and it is closed to common sense after heavy rain.

location: Snake Gorge (Snake Canyon), Wadi Bani Awf
alt: Rugged rock gorge cutting through the mountains at Snake Gorge in Wadi Bani Awf
caption: Snake Gorge in Wadi Bani Awf, a rocky gorge of pools, boulders and short swims below the Hajar peaks. It is descended with a local guide who reads the water level: confident swimming is needed and the water is cold in March.

location: Balad Sayt (Bilad Sayt), Wilayat of Rustaq
alt: Palm garden and dry-stone terrace walls with houses on the hill above at Balad Sayt
caption: Palm gardens and dry-stone terrace walls below the houses of Balad Sayt, set at the foot of a 1,100 m cliff. Guesthouses and camping on the edge of the village make it the base for the first two nights.

location: Misfat Al Abriyyin, Wilayat of Al Hamra
alt: Old mud-brick houses and palm terraces of Misfat Al Abriyyin on a rocky slope
caption: Misfat Al Abriyyin, a mountainside village of stone and mud-brick houses with irrigated palm and banana terraces below. A short walk along its narrow lanes and water channels breaks the drive up to Jebel Shams.

commonsFile: File:Step Gardens of Jebel Akhdar - Oman.jpg
location: Terraces on the Jebel Akhdar plateau, Ad Dakhiliyah
alt: Stepped terraced gardens on the slopes of Jebel Akhdar
caption: The stepped gardens of Jebel Akhdar, the Green Mountain, where terraces fed by stone channels grow walnuts, apricots and pomegranates at about 2,000 m. The plateau is reached by a police-checked 4x4-only road and anchors the second half of the route.

commonsFile: File:Jebel Akhdar – abandoned villages of Wadi Bani Habib.jpg
alt: Abandoned stone village on the wall of the Wadi Bani Habib gorge
caption: The abandoned village in Wadi Bani Habib, wrapped around the bottom of a gorge below the plateau edge. Orchards beside the ruins are still worked, which makes it a walk through a living landscape rather than a ruin visit.

commonsFile: File:Bat Al Ayn Beehive Tombs UNESCO Oman.jpg
location: Bat, Al-Khutm and Al-Ayn, Ad Dhahirah Governorate
alt: Row of Bronze Age beehive tombs on a ridge below a golden mountain wall near Ibri
caption: Beehive tombs of the Bat, Al-Khutm and Al-Ayn necropolis below the Jebel Misht cliffs, inscribed by UNESCO in 1988. Dating to the third millennium BC, the group lies near Ibri, far from the usual circuit, and is the trip's archaeology day.

location: Al-Ayn beehive tombs, near Ibri, Ad Dhahirah
alt: Row of weathered stone beehive tombs on a ridge at Al-Ayn
caption: The Al-Ayn tombs line a ridge with the Jebel Misht massif behind them. Late afternoon light is the reason to visit at the end of the day rather than at midday, and there are no ticket booths or crowds.

location: Nakhal Fort, Al Batinah South Governorate
alt: Whitewashed Nakhal Fort on a rocky hill beside a palm oasis
caption: Nakhal Fort, on a rock above the oasis town at the northern foot of Jebel Akhdar. It is the stop between the plateau and Rustaq, with the Ain Thowarah hot spring a short drive away.
